articles.t: GTA 6 convinced me: I'm okay with 30 FPS gaming, and you should be too
articles.chapeau: The release of GTA VI is once again igniting the 30 FPS debate, and I'm on the side of pushing boundaries. Do kids even know what Crysis is?
articles.txt:
With this week’s console release of Grand Theft Auto VI , the internet is once again debating whether or not gaming at 30 frames per second is acceptable in modern times. Hell, there are plenty of people (including several on staff at PCWorld) who are dead-set on waiting for a PC release to unlock higher frame rates. And I’ve seen far too many forum threads full of high-and-mighty PC gamers turning their noses up at console peasants for accepting “subpar” performance.
Well, here’s the thing: I’m absolutely fine playing GTA VI on console at a smoooooooth 30 because it’s doing something that I’ve always appreciated about bleeding edge games — it’s pushing the boundaries of available hardware. And in the case of GTA VI it’s pushing the boundaries for normal gamers, not just the elite.
Welcome to The Full Nerd newsletter—your weekly dose of hardware talk from the enthusiasts at PCWorld. Missed the surprising topics on our YouTube podcast or the latest news from across the web? You’re in the right place.
Want this newsletter to come directly to your inbox? Sign up on our website !
I started following the PC gaming scene (and the late, great Gordon Mah Ung) around 2007, at a time when Crysis dominated the discourse. Everyone was absolutely losing their mind at the level of detail in the game. It was a badge of pride that the game was so demanding that it melted even the best GPU of it’s day: the Nvidia GeForce 8800 GTX. On top of that, the graphics were so intense and the gameplay so precise that the thought of Crysis running on a console just didn’t make sense.
That game, and others like DOOM 3 , pushed hardware forward in ways we simply don’t see anymore. These experiences were limited to the small few who could afford high end computers, rather than the wider console audience, and it gave people something to aspire to.
PC gamers who had high end rigs were able to gloat over their console friends, and they felt justified in sitting atop the gaming food chain. Not me though. My computer at the time was a budget-ass eMachine and all I could do was listen to the guys on GFW Radio and Maximum PC’s No BS Podcast wax poetically about what it was like to play such generation-defining games, with a dream that one day I could have a PC powerful enough to experience it myself. By the time I actually built my first PC, it was equipped with a GeForce GTX 460 that still wasn’t able to play Crysis the way it was meant to be experienced — but I could at least try!
I remember it being choppy as hell, and yet I still loved it.
We lived in a different era. Even though PC gaming was a very expensive hobby, back in those days the idea of hitting 30fps on a 1280×1024 monitor at high settings was commonplace. This was partly because tentpole games pushed the boundaries of what the hardware was capable of, introducing new technologies that had tangible benefits. Transport back in time to the Maximum PC offices and try to turn up your nose at sub-60 frame rates and you’d probably get laughed out of the room for being a snob. Yes, there were plenty of 60fps experiences to be had at the time but low framerates were more widely accepted, especially as we moved into the Xbox 360 era.
But in today’s day and age, sub-60 frame rates are routinely mocked and ridiculed, and somehow that’s just become normal in PC gaming spheres. Yes, we’re starting to hit walls of diminishing returns when it comes to visual technology, and yes, high refresh rate monitors are cheap and ubiquitous, and yes, everyone understands that “frames win games,” but I think we should still be celebrating achievements that push new boundaries, not mocking people who get to experience it.
Grand Theft Auto has become such a monstrous series in it’s own right, and what Rockstar achieved in GTA VI on relatively outdated hardware (modern consoles have AMD’s older Zen 2 and RDNA 2 architectures inside) deserves to be applauded. This might be the first time someone will get a chance to experience full ray-traced global illumination (or ray-traced shadows if they have a PS5 Pro), for example — a technology that makes a monumental impact to real-time lighting and is well worth the performance trade-off.

articles.txt:
Sorti le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series, GTA VI est classé PEGI 18 : il est donc déconseillé aux moins de 18 ans. Mais cette classification n’est pas une interdiction légale en France, plutôt une recommandation, accompagnée de pictogrammes qui détaillent le contenu du jeu. Violence, sexe, drogue, langage, achats intégrés : voici tout ce que dit la fiche officielle PEGI de Grand Theft Auto VI, pour permettre à chaque parent de prendre sa décision en connaissance de cause.
GTA VI (ou GTA 6) est classé PEGI 18 : son contenu est jugé adapté aux adultes uniquement.
Cette classification s’explique par trois types de contenus : violence très explicite, thèmes sexuels explicites et consommation de drogues illégales. Le jeu propose aussi des achats intégrés, facultatifs.
En France, PEGI est une recommandation, pas une interdiction : aucune loi n’empêche un mineur de jouer à un jeu PEGI 18.
Les PS5 et Xbox Series intègrent un contrôle parental capable de filtrer les jeux selon leur classification PEGI.
Non, pas au sens de la loi. Le nouveau jeu de Rockstar Games a reçu la classification PEGI 18, la plus élevée de l’échelle, ce qui signifie que son accès est recommandé aux adultes uniquement et qu’il est jugé inadapté aux personnes âgées de moins de 18 ans. Mais en France, cette mention reste une recommandation, et non une interdiction.
Depuis le milieu des années 2010, PEGI est le système de classification officiellement reconnu par l’État pour les jeux vidéo, homologué par le ministère de l’Intérieur. Pour autant, sa vocation est d’alerter et d’informer les parents, et il ne fait en aucun cas office d’interdiction formelle. Concrètement, aucune loi n’interdit à un mineur de jouer à GTA VI, ni à un adulte de le lui offrir.
Ce n’est d’ailleurs pas le cas partout en Europe : au Royaume-Uni, par exemple, les classifications PEGI 12, 16 et 18 ont force de loi, et la vente d’un jeu PEGI 18 à un mineur y est interdite. En France, la décision revient donc entièrement aux parents. Et c’est justement pour l’éclairer que la classification existe.
PEGI (pour Pan European Game Information) est le système européen de classification des jeux vidéo par âge. Créé en 2003 à l’initiative des éditeurs de jeux vidéo européens, il est aujourd’hui utilisé dans plus d’une trentaine de pays, et ses logos s’affichent aussi bien sur les boîtes de jeux que sur les boutiques en ligne des consoles.
Une classification par âge, symbolisée par un chiffre sur fond de couleur : PEGI 3 et PEGI 7 (vert), PEGI 12 et PEGI 16 (orange), PEGI 18 (rouge).
Des descripteurs de contenu, sous forme de pictogrammes, qui précisent pourquoi le jeu a reçu sa classification : violence, langage grossier, peur, sexe, drogues, discrimination, jeux de hasard et achats intégrés.
Ce sont les éditeurs qui déclarent le contenu de leur jeu via un questionnaire détaillé, mais la classification est ensuite contrôlée par deux organismes indépendants, le NICAM aux Pays-Bas et le VSC au Royaume-Uni. Les jeux qui visent une classification 16 ou 18 sont systématiquement visionnés avant que la recommandation d’âge ne soit délivrée.
Point important : PEGI juge uniquement le contenu. La classification ne tient compte ni du niveau de difficulté du jeu, ni des aptitudes nécessaires pour y jouer. Un jeu PEGI 18 n’est donc pas un jeu « pour les grands » parce qu’il serait plus compliqué, mais parce que ce qu’il montre est destiné à un public adulte.
Pour celles et ceux qui ne connaissent pas la licence, GTA (pour Grand Theft Auto, l’expression anglo-saxonne désignant le vol de véhicule) est l’une des séries les plus vendues de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Depuis ses débuts en 1997, elle est connue pour son ton satirique et pour son contenu destiné aux adultes. Son précédent épisode, GTA V, sorti en 2013, était d’ailleurs lui aussi classé PEGI 18.
Développé par Rockstar Games et édité par Take-Two Interactive, GTA VI est un jeu d’action-aventure en monde ouvert : on peut s’y déplacer librement dans un vaste environnement, sans parcours imposé. L’aventure se déroule dans Leonida, un État fictif inspiré de la Floride.
On y incarne, en vue à la troisième personne, Jason Duval ou Lucia Caminos, deux criminels qui se retrouvent impliqués dans un complot à la suite d’un braquage raté. articles.t: Was GTA 6 worth the wait? | Joanne Young’s courage | Ukraine strikes Crimea bridge | Myanmar genocide
articles.chapeau: Your Week In 4: Hand-picked insightful, inspiring and compelling reports from Channel 4 News this week.
articles.txt:
Channel 4 News Nov 20, 2026 Share Welcome to Your Week In 4 , your quick, curated catch-up on the week’s standout stories from Channel 4 News .
Each week, our team hand-picks four of the most compelling reports - from in-depth investigations and powerful interviews to moments that sparked national conversation.
Whether you missed them the first time or just want to see the highlights that matter most, Your Week In 4 brings the best of Channel 4 News straight to your inbox - sharp, insightful, inspiring and ready to read and watch in minutes.
GTA 6 is finally out - was it worth the wait? How did Grand Theft Auto become bigger than just a game?
Thirteen years in the making, GTA 6 has been dubbed the biggest release of all time.
It’s thought to have cost more $1bn to produce. And it cost businesses millions more, as players across the world booked the day off for what might just be the most hyped launch in history.
In this episode of the breakdown , we take a deep dive into the famous and controversial franchise and speak to YouTuber Jelle van Vucht, who runs the Jelly YouTube channel.
We look at how Grand Theft Auto became a billion-dollar, cross-generational phenomenon, and whether - after 13 years of waiting for the sequel - anything can actually live up to all this hype.
Warning: viewers may find some of the details in this report distressing
Joanne Young is a woman whose name will now go down alongside that of Gisele Pelicot for being a symbol of courage.
This week's conviction of the four men who sexually abused her while she was drugged by her husband has echoes of that case in France two years ago which resonated around the world.
Gisele Pelicot said back then that shame must change sides. Joanne Young, who waived her anonymity and was commended by the judge for her bravery, embodied that promise.
If you've been affected by the details of Joanne Young's case, then help is available. Visit channel4.com/support
A Ukrainian drone blew up part of Russia's vital Kerch bridge linking Crimea to the Russian Federation this week. On the same night, the Russians targeted bridges in Kyiv.
The strike badly damaged the Crimean bridge prized by President Putin, with a section collapsing into the Kerch Strait and damaging the rail bridge next to it, according to Ukrainian officials. It was Ukraine's second strike on the bridge in two days.
Russian forces also hit two major bridges in Kyiv, along with other critical infrastructure in the Ukrainian capital.
They also attacked facilities in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia , and Dnipro.
The International Court of Justice court ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
It was the first time a state has ever been found guilty of the crime by an international court.
In 2017, a violent Myanmar military campaign forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya in Rakhine State across the border into Bangladesh.
The influx created the massive camps in Cox’s Bazar which house over 1 million refugees.

articles.t: Burger King, JBL, U... Ces marques qui s'emparent de GTA VI pour promouvoir leurs produits
articles.chapeau: Si les influenceurs, médias spécialisés et joueurs amateurs ont déjà commencé à bien investir GTA VI depuis sa sortie dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, les marques s'en sont aussi largement emparées. Une stratégie nommée "newsjacking". Tour d'horizon des enseignes qui ont saisi cette occasion pour...
articles.txt:
Après 13 ans d'attente depuis le dernier volet, le jeu vidéo "Grand Theft Auto" ou plus communément appelé GTA VI est sorti dans la nuit de ce mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre sur Playstation 5 et Xbox Series. Depuis plus de 24 heures, les extraits vidéo se multiplient sur les réseaux sociaux, tout comme les lives de parties en direct par des créateurs de contenus.
Le jeu s'offre même déjà la note de 99 sur 100 sur l'agrégateur Metacritic, devenant le jeu le mieux noté de l'histoire rapporté au nombre de tests. GTA VI serait, par ailleurs, en lice dans plusieurs catégories des Game Awards, dont celle du "Jeu de l'année 2026", selon nos confrères de BFM Tech .
Au-delà des influenceurs, des médias spécialisés ou encore des joueurs amateurs, c'est un phénomène mondial dont se sont emparés de nombreuses marques. Le producteur du jeu, Rockstar Games, a ainsi noué des collaborations commerciales officielles avec quelques unes d'entre elles comme PlayStation, Netflix , Spotify, YouTube ou encore Nike.
En revanche, d'autres marques, qui ne sont pas partenaires du jeu, ont profité de la tendance pour s'exposer ou mettre en avant l'un de leurs produits. C'est ce que l'on appelle du "newsjacking". Une stratégie qui peut se montrer efficace en terme d'image et d'attrait de nouveaux clients, surtout pour des marques proche de l'univers du jeu.
On peut par exemple citer les constructeurs automobiles Hyundai, BMW et Toyota, mais aussi Yamaha avec sa gamme de scooter. Les déplacements en voiture ou en deux roues étant très caractéristiques de GTA depuis ses débuts.

articles.t: De Dua Lipa à Keith Richards… Les stars se bousculent dans la bande originale de « GTA 6 »
articles.chapeau: music play - « Grand Theft Auto VI : The Album », une compil' de trente-quatre titres originaux de stars mondiales, met du bon son dans les oreilles des gamers
articles.txt:
« GTA VI, The Album » est disponible sur les plateformes de streaming. music play - « Grand Theft Auto VI : The Album », une compil' de trente-quatre titres originaux de stars mondiales, met du bon son dans les oreilles des gamers
La musique pèse dans le game. Depuis minuit, « GTA 6 », est à la disposition des gamers du monde entier sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series. Le nouvel épisode de la saga « Grand Theft Auto » s'accompagne de musiques inédites d'artistes de renom.
Et dès le lancement du jeu sur consoles, le générique se fait entendre. Starting From Zero , titre original du duo français Justice avec Michael McDonald au chant, membre des Doobie Brothers, accompagne en bruit de fond des joueuses et des joueurs déjà conquis . Le morceau se retrouve dans un disque de trente-quatre titres inédits, Grand Theft Auto VI : The Album , disponible sur les plateformes.
Parmi les autres créations à découvrir, Don't Chart de Cardi B , Go Easy de Dua Lipa , Crazy For You de Lana Del Rey ou encore Blood In Your Eyes de Tove Lo. Dans cet opus produit par Rockstar et le label Atlantic Records, on peut également savourer des titres de Burna Boy, Camila Cabello, Étienne de Crécy, Fred Again, Future, Tame Impala, Travis Scott, Zara Larsson et même de Keith Richards, des Rolling Stones . Et le succès est déjà au rendez-vous. Sorti avant le lancement de GTA 6 , Suzuki du groupe Fuerza Regida compte plus de 70 millions d'écoutes sur Spotify .
Au-delà de cette trentaine de titres, les stars de la French touch, Gaspard Augé et Xavier de Rosnay ont d'ores et déjà œuvré sur un second album, baptisé Grand Theft Auto VI : Original Score », dont la sortie est prévue le 11 décembre.

articles.txt:
Sometimes it’s hard to say goodbye. Especially if it’s a video game called Grand Theft Auto 6 that you’ve dumped dozens of hours into. The main story, though, should take between 50-80 hours to complete. But if you’ve grown very fond of Lucia and Jason, you might be worried that you won’t be able to play following the rolling of the end credits.
Not to fear: you can keep playing GTA 6 after the story ends . You will be returned to the point before you triggered the final stretch of the game once you roll the credits. After that, you will be able to change Lucia and Jason’s relationship to try and trigger a different ending, stop maxing out your savings, and maybe even become Irredeemable , for a laugh.
Once you finish the story, you will then be able to track how much of the total game you’ve beaten. For reference, we have 140 hours and only 78% total completion. There’s so, so much to see and do around Leonida once you beat the story that it’s surely impossible without some kind of guide. We’d actually estimate that finding all animals, doing all stunt jumps, collecting every card etc could take you way beyond 200 hours. If you’re hunting for the Platinum…good luck.
On top of tracking 100% completion, you will also be able to unlock and use cheats , though you will still need to beat challenges in order to actually use them.
So, yeah, don’t worry about the game locking you out before the end of the game. It’s not the original release of Fallout 3 anymore. You can still cause havoc and complete side missions until you’ve had your fill without having to sweat the big stuff.
Until that time, here’s how to track down the rarest car in the game and save yourself some serious money on repairs .

articles.t: GTA 6 Caused a Mass 'Migration' of Over 2 Million People
articles.chapeau: Who else has moved to New Zealand?
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 was released on Thursday, Nov. 19... officially. Millions of players around the world actually got to play it on Nov. 18 by moving to New Zealand. Well, not actually. Players just changed their account's region to New Zealand. It's a known trick that lets gamers access digital games before release when companies opt for a staggered launch, as with GTA 6 . Reports indicate that, in the UK and the US, 2 million Xbox players used the New Zealand trick to gain access to GTA 6 early. And that doesn't even account for the rest of the world or PlayStation players.
The report doesn't mention how many PlayStation 5 players resorted to this method because the process involves jumping through several hoops, so the number is likely much lower. You need a whole new PSN account, then enable game sharing, and purchase GTA 6 through the NZ account using New Zealand dollars. On Xbox, you just have to change your console's region. For many, it's just not worth the time and effort, and they'd rather wait a few hours.
Additionally, given the hype around the release, it wouldn't be surprising for fans in every country to have followed this method — even players in neighboring Australia, who had to wait an extra full hour. All in all, with about 20 million copies pre-ordered , the migration must've included much more than 2 million people.
Image: Rockstar Games The biggest time difference was for players in the US, who were able to play GTA 6 21 hours before its scheduled launch in their region. It almost sounds too good to be true, so you might be wondering if this is a bannable offense. The truth is, it's all a bit iffy. Terms of service are a serious matter in the gaming world. Technically, Xbox and Sony don't want players to circumvent access restrictions to software or provide false information when creating an account. However, neither company seems to want to go as far as punishing players for playing a game a few hours early — especially when they've been waiting as long as they have for Grand Theft Auto 6 . At least for now.

articles.t: Au Japon, GTA 6 est censuré pour éviter la nudité et une part de représentation de la violence
articles.chapeau: Plus GTA devient réaliste, plus il faut s’attendre à ce que certains pays soient plus stricts sur ce qui est affiché à l’écran. [...]
articles.txt:
Plus GTA devient réaliste, plus il faut s’attendre à ce que certains pays soient plus stricts sur ce qui est affiché à l’écran. C’est notamment le cas du Japon, qui possède un système de régulation qui fait beaucoup parler de lui et qui a déjà mis en place certaines censures, comme sur Dispatch ou sur The Callisto Protocol , pour ne citer que des exemples récents. Comme on pouvait s’y attendre, GTA 6 connaît le même destin.
« Cachez ces fesses que je ne devrais pas voir » Depuis la sortie de GTA 6 hier, plusieurs internautes japonais partagent des photos ou des vidéos du jeu pour montrer que la version vendue au Japon n’est pas tout à fait la même que celle que l’on peut retrouver en Occident . En témoigne par exemple un screenshot partagé par Genki sur Twitter, où l’on peut voir Jason être affublé d’un slip (assez échancré tout de même) au lieu d’avoir les fesses à l’air, lorsqu’il prend sa douche.
Ce n’est pas la seule représentation de nudité qui est gommée ici, puisque le site GameSpark (relayé par VGC ) a montré que cette censure s’applique également à la violence affichée dans le jeu, en montrant moins de sang et en supprimant les décapitations. Chose que vous pouvez vous-mêmes désactiver si l’envie vous en prend dans les paramètres, mais le public japonais n’a pas cette liberté d’afficher cela ou non. Ce degré de censure est placé pour que le jeu obtienne la certification CERO Z, qui est l’équivalent de notre PEGI 18, afin que le jeu soit quand même proposé à la vente.
Rien qui ne gâche vraiment l’aventure dans la mesure où tout cela est uniquement esthétique, mais cela ne devrait pas ravir tout le monde.

articles.t: GTA 6 : après Jason et Lucia tout nus, Cyberleek promet la version piratée du jeu complet pour le 23 novembre
articles.chapeau: Le leaker qui a pourri la promo de GTA 6 tout l’automne n’avait pas dit son dernier mot. Et cette fois, ce ne sont plus quelques vidéos.
articles.txt:
Le leaker qui a pourri la promo de GTA 6 tout l’automne n’avait pas dit son dernier mot. Et cette fois, ce ne sont plus quelques vidéos.
Est-ce que vous saviez que GTA 6 est enfin sorti hier sur PS5 et Xbox Series ? Oui, difficile de passer à côté hein. On aurait pu croire que la saga des fuites était derrière nous, puisque le jeu est désormais dans les mains de tout le monde. Sauf que Cyberleek, le compte anonyme qui a diffusé des extraits volés pendant des mois, a choisi le jour de la sortie pour refaire surface.
Pour ceux qui auraient raté les épisodes précédents : depuis août, Cyberleek a publié des dizaines de vidéos de gameplay en amont de la sortie, toujours avec le même deal. Les fuites continuent tant qu’un meme coin à son nom, le $CYBERLEEK, prend de la valeur. Début octobre, il avait frappé fort avec une vidéo de 25 minutes où l’on voyait Jason et Lucia entièrement nus, y compris en cinématique . Il y faisait même apparaître un tank de nulle part, ce qui montrait clairement qu’il avait accès au menu debug d’une build jouable.
L’objectif à l’époque était une capitalisation de 30 millions de dollars . Entre temps, la cryptomonnaie s’est effondrée et Cyberleek a disparu à la mi-octobre avec un message d’adieu en trois parties. Rockstar et Take-Two n’ont visiblement jamais réussi à mettre la main sur lui.
Le jour de la sortie du jeu, son site a publié un nouveau message. Cyberleek y affirme diffuser par torrent une build Xbox complète de GTA 6 datée de novembre 2026, qui pèse environ 209 Go , donc grosso modo la taille du jeu sur console. Il manque cependant un fichier, et pas des moindres : l’exécutable principal, sans lequel rien ne se lance.
Ce fichier ne sortira que si le $CYBERLEEK atteint 15 millions de dollars de capitalisation, ou le 23 novembre quoi qu’il arrive. Le leaker assure aussi que la communauté arrivera à émuler cette version Xbox en moins d’une semaine, à plus de 30 fps. Si ça ne marche pas, il promet de s’attaquer à une build PS5.
Il faut quand même garder du recul, puisque l’émulation d’un jeu Xbox Series sur PC n’a rien d’une simple formalité , donc la promesse d’une version PC piratée en une semaine relève surtout du marketing de crypto.
Si vous êtes tenté de jeter un œil, sachez que ce genre de fuite attire les escrocs. Des chercheurs ont déjà repéré de faux installeurs « GTA 6 PC » qui servaient en réalité à installer des infostealers, ces logiciels qui récupèrent vos mots de passe . Un exécutable trouvé sur un forum quelques jours après une fuite non vérifiée, c’est exactement ce qu’il faut éviter. Le $CYBERLEEK s’est déjà effondré une fois, donc acheter cette crypto revient surtout à financer le prochain chantage.

articles.t: Bigfoot, jet-ski avec un chien, doomscroll… C’est aussi ça « GTA 6 »
articles.chapeau: « GTA 6 » regorge d'activités et de situations aussi absurdes qu'insolites. On vous fait une petite liste qui rajoute un peu de piment et de folie au jeu
articles.txt:
Qui a dit que dans GTA 6 il fallait forcément braquer une épicerie ou participer à une course-poursuite avec la police ? C’est connu, la franchise est une usine à activités insolites et farfelues en tout genre. Et dans ce nouvel opus, le développeur Rockstar Games a poussé le bouchon encore plus loin.
Au milieu du chaos habituel, une multitude de petites expériences aussi improbables que décalées attendent les joueurs. Une simple balade à Vice City peut donc se transformer en une journée totalement absurde. On vous propose quelques activités à réaliser qui risquent bien de nous faire perdre des heures.
Bon ça reste du GTA , il faut quand même pouvoir voler des trucs. Mais si, pour une fois, on oubliait les hélicoptères et les petits ULM pour prendre les commandes d’un véritable avion de ligne ? Imaginez-vous dans le cockpit d’un appareil commercial, avec des centaines de passagers à bord, en train de survoler la Floride fictive. Bon, connaissant les joueurs, on ne garantit pas que l’atterrissage se déroule sans incident… Dans GTA 5, on pouvait aussi voler des rafales militaires. Cette franchise nous permet vraiment de conduire tout et n’importe quoi.
Pas de flingues ou de grenades, GTA 6 mise aussi sur des moments beaucoup plus mignons. Parmi les scènes qui ont particulièrement retenu l’attention, on retrouve la possibilité de faire du jet-ski accompagné de son chien. Oui, même dans un univers rempli de violence, il faut savoir prendre du temps pour son meilleur compagnon à quatre pattes. Le pire c’est que le chien est dans son univers. Petites lunettes, poils au vent, on reconnaît les animaux qui profitent à fond de leur vie.
Les mystères et les légendes urbaines font partie de l’ADN de GTA . Et GTA 6 perpétue bien cette tradition avec une rencontre pour le moins inattendue : celle du Bigfoot. Il était déjà là dans GTA 5 , et certains joueurs l’ont déjà aperçu un court instant dans les tréfonds de Vice City. Il faut dire qu’entre les marécages, les forêts et les coins reculés de la map du jeu, le terrain est idéal pour cacher quelques créatures mystérieuses. Ça donne surtout envie de quitter les grandes avenues de Vice City pour partir à la chasse aux phénomènes paranormaux.
Bienvenue en Floride ! Finalement, il n’y a pas plus américain que ça. Dans GTA 6 , la police n’est pas forcément le plus grand danger. Fidèles à Miami, les alligators font aussi partie du décor du jeu. Et évidemment, certains joueurs ne résisteront pas à l’envie de les provoquer. Se retrouver face à un reptile de plusieurs mètres dans un marécage promet quelques séquences mémorables.
Vous voulez vous détacher de votre téléphone pour éviter de scroller ? Eh bien GTA 6 vous replonge dans votre addiction. C’est peut-être l’une des activités les plus modernes et les plus absurdes du jeu. On peut désormais passer son temps à faire défiler du contenu sur les réseaux sociaux virtuels. Comme dans leur lit, les joueurs peuvent regarder des vidéos virales et des publications improbables. Le jeu semble vouloir reproduire nos mauvaises habitudes numériques. Le plus drôle ? On pourrait presque passer plus de temps à regarder l’écran de son personnage qu’à explorer le monde qui nous entoure. Finalement, même dans GTA, impossible d’échapper au doomscrolling.
Et si la meilleure activité de GTA 6 consistait tout simplement à ne rien faire ? Se lever, prendre sa voiture, aller faire quelques courses, manger un morceau, faire de la musculation, se promener sur la plage ou simplement faire bronzette. Rockstar a toujours excellé dans la création de mondes vivants, remplis de détails et de situations spontanées.
Alors, on vous propose de consacrer une journée entière à vivre comme un habitant normal de Vice City. Pas de braquage, pas de fusillade, pas de course-poursuite. Juste une journée ordinaire… jusqu’à ce qu’un événement complètement improbable vienne tout gâcher.

articles.t: GTA 6 Leaker 'Cyberleek' Reportedly Threatens to Release the XBOX Build
articles.chapeau: The infamous GTA 6 leaker has reportedly threatened to release the game's XBOX build, which can seemingly be emulated on PC.
articles.txt:
A new report reveals that the infamous GTA 6 leaker ‘Cyberleek’ has threatened to release almost the entire XBOX build of the game.
This isn’t the first time the leaker has threatened to do so; a month ago , Cyberleek said the same thing, revealing that if their cryptocurrency’s market value crossed $30 million, they would release a playable build. However, he cashed out soon after, and we haven’t heard much from the leaker since, other than some inappropriate Lucia leaks . Now, the leaker has decreased the milestone people need to reach for the build to be released.
A new report by IGN informs players about the alleged GTA 6 XBOX build drop from Cyberleek. It seems that the leaker has dumped all the files of the XBOX build apart from the .exe file, which they claim to be a “full November 2026 build of GTA.” The leaker adds that this build would allow the community to emulate the game on PC and have it run way higher than its 30 FPS lock on console. If that build doesn’t work, Cyberleek will work towards getting a PS5 build to the players.
At the time of writing, the market cap of Cyberleek’s meme coin sits at around $1.5 million, and it seems very unlikely that it can jump to $15 million in the next few days. So it seems like November 23 could be the day they eventually drop GTA 6’s XBOX build, but whether they have the XBOX build in hand is a different question altogether. If they do, it could be a big problem for Rockstar, considering the PC release date hasn’t been announced yet.
Players will just have to wait and see whether what Cyberleek is alleging is indeed true, and the wait is not long, as November 23 arrives in 3 days.

articles.t: Should I buy a PS5 or Xbox to play 'GTA 6'?
articles.chapeau: 'Grand Theft Auto VI' is easily the most-anticipated video game of all time.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto VI is out now, if you hadn't heard. If you're not playing it but are reading this, we can guess why.
By that, we mean you might not have a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series console at the ready to play the highly anticipated release. If that's the case, you're going to miss out on the biggest gaming launch of the year — and possibly all time. FOMO is a natural human reaction to these sorts of things, and here at Mashable, we fully understand the pain of not being sure whether or not you should buy a console just for GTA 6 .
The primary and most obvious reason to buy a console for GTA 6 is that it's the only real way to play it at launch. There is technically another way that we'll cover in a little while, but for all intents and purposes, you cannot have the same experience everyone else is having without buying a PS5 or Xbox Series console.
By all accounts , GTA 6 is a pretty fantastic video game. You probably wouldn't want to miss out on that. What are you going to do while everyone else is having an amazing time parading through Leonida, read books? Come on, that sounds boring.
One thing that's also worth remembering is that other video games exist. A lot of them, in fact. If you buy a PS5 or Xbox Series console, you'll have access to the last six years of current-gen releases, some of which are extremely good. They might even be better than GTA 6 ! As a fun bonus, through the magic of backward compatibility, ports, remasters, and remakes, you'll also be able to play countless video games from previous generations of hardware, too.
Lastly, both consoles (at least the models with disc drives) work as 4K Blu-ray players, if you're into collecting physical versions of movies. That's cool, too.
Both consoles have been hard to find in stock (thanks in large part to GTA 6 ), but the Xbox Series S and PS5 Digital Edition are both in stock at Amazon, as of this writing. If you're not sure whether to buy a PS5 or the Xbox Series X/S, keep scrolling for a breakdown of the pros and cons.
First, foremost, in the biggest, boldest font you can imagine: You shouldn't buy a console just for GTA 6 because they're stupid expensive these days.
Both Xbox and PlayStation have recently increased the prices of their consoles due to real-world economic concerns . The cheapest model right now is a $499 Xbox Series S, and Rockstar hasn't shown us that version of the game yet, leading to speculation that the game is better on PS5 , which starts at $599. If you want the best possible version at launch, you'll need a PS5 Pro, which costs $899 — and is currently out of stock at most retailers.
In other words, there just isn't a particularly affordable way to play GTA 6 traditionally at launch, unless you already own the hardware.
There are, of course, other reasons to not get a console for GTA 6 . There exists a slim likelihood that you won't like the game, though so far, most people who have played it have come away with positive impressions. It also won't have an online component at launch, and no one knows when it will get one. For a lot of people, GTA Online is the only GTA experience that matters, and that audience will have very little to do in the new game until some nebulous point in the future when Rockstar decides to cater to them.
Maybe you just don't care that much about non- GTA video games, either. If that's the case, it's hard to recommend spending this much money on a box that will only play one game.
There was a lot of anxiety on the internet prior to the game's launch surrounding the potential differences between the different console versions. The good news is that the game is out and has been fully tested by experts, and the verdict is that you almost can't go wrong with GTA 6 on any platform.
Digital Foundry is an outlet and YouTube channel that offers expert-level tech analysis of games, and they have a fairly comprehensive guide to the different console versions of GTA 6 . According to DF, both the PS5 and Series X versions run at the same resolution and target the same frame rate, with some performance dips on both in more intense sequences. articles.t: Cyberleek returns and threatens to release free pirate version of GTA 6
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 leaker Cyberleek has reappeared with a development build of Rockstar's sequel on Xbox, which will apparently be released next week.
articles.txt:
Nobody’s favourite GTA 6 leaker has returned with a development build of the game, which will apparently be released online next week.
While GTA 6’s launch has gone by relatively smoothly, minus all the work absences , the road to this point has been a turbulent ride to say the least.
Beyond all the delays , GTA 6 has been a prime target for hackers . The most notable culprit this year is a group, or individual, known as Cyberleek, who began releasing gameplay clips in August from an early build of the game, while benefitting from the videos via crypto donations.
Cyberleek’s last appearance was in October, when they threatened to ruin the end of GTA 6 if Rockstar took legal action. At the time, they said the ‘leeks stop here’, suggesting the whole ordeal was over, but now they have reappeared, like a stubborn crypto cockroach.
As shared on Reddit , Cyberleek has allegedly released the ‘full November 2026 build’ of GTA 6 on Xbox on his website, in a file named ‘XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026)’. However, the executable file is missing, so you can’t actually play it yet.
In a statement, Cyberleek claims the executable file is ‘held on a countdown’ and will be released on November 23 no matter what, but it will be released earlier if their crypto coin reaches a $15 million (£11.4 million) cap.
Sign up to the GameCentral newsletter for the latest GTA 6 news, reviews of new games you should play and exclusive analysis of the biggest stories of the week.
A post on their website reads: ‘It is done. CL holds the full November 2026 build of GTA 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one – the main executable – held on a countdown. Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to pre-order for a reason. This is one of the reasons.’
They added: ‘The countdown is the timer for the final file. Zero, and the executable drops, no conditions. Unless the CYBERLEEK token reaches 15 million market cap first – then it drops immediately. 30 million was too ambitious; half that seems fair.
‘CL asks for support. If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, CL will work to get a PS5 build — a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar.’
Being a development build means it’s not the final version of the game but is presumably the same version he was recording for his videos, with access to the game’s debug menu that gives you control of things like spawning tanks and making the main characters nude.
Having this be accessible to anyone would obviously be bad news for Rockstar, but it’s unclear if the files are genuine (or if they will be riddled with malware). The Xbox build they have is around 200GB, so it is close to the 212GB size of the final game.
Either way, this feels like a last desperate attempt for crypto donations, at a time when barely anyone is paying attention because GTA 6 is actually out in the wild, across PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
We’ll have to see if this build comes to fruition later this month, and how quickly Rockstar’s lawyers will jump into action if it does.

articles.t: GTA 6 Actor Says Rockstar Made Their Non-Binary Character Unkillable
articles.chapeau: Jesse James Rose speaks about their experience on set for GTA 6
articles.txt:
The state of Leonida has thousands of inhabitants, each one with their own story. One of them is Cygnus, not only Vice City's museum curator, but also the first non-binary character in Grand Theft Auto history. In a detailed Instagram post , actor Jesse James Rose revealed that they played Cygnus and shared their experience working with Rockstar Games on the set of GTA 6 .
Grand Theft Auto allows players to lead a hectic life of crime with lots of killing, shooting, and stealing, but of course, that doesn't reflect the values of the people who made it. Rose began filming for GTA 6 three years before its release and spent weeks on set. They shared that the set of Grand Theft Auto 6 was among the most inclusive and caring sets they'd worked on. However, at the time, they had no idea what they were filming for; to ensure confidentiality, they had to sign 17 different NDAs.
Considering that Jesse James Rose spent weeks filming, Cygnus is expected to play a role in the story of GTA 6 or a major sidequest, so players will likely encounter them at some point in the campaign. To prevent anti-trans violence in Grand Theft Auto 6 , Rockstar assured Rose that players would not be able to harm Cygnus in-game.
The trans actor (who now uses she/they pronouns but preferred they/them pronouns at the time) said the developers made sure to portray the non-binary character Cygnus accurately and respectfully. Rockstar relied exclusively on motion capture to create Cygnus, highlighting that it would be impossible for AI to come up with the same faces as a real person. Given the growing use of AI in the video game industry, this stood out to Rose: "Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labor to preserve the integrity of the game."
While Jesse James Rose played the first non-binary character in Grand Theft Auto, they were not the only trans person working on the game. Trans people held other crucial roles in the making of GTA 6 , such as writers, designers, and more. Rose notes that although they were "paid well" and are still "thrilled to be a part of this project," they stand by their values and continue to advocate for workplace unionization, workers' rights, and fair compensation, which have been issues at Rockstar Games .

articles.t: GTA 6's Main Story Progression Has One Requirement That Could Surprise Players - SVG
articles.chapeau: One requirement for the main story progression of Grand Theft Auto VI is different from previous games, but ends up being a wise decision.
articles.txt:
Rockstar Games Add SVG on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover WARNING : There are slight spoilers for the story of "GTA 6" in this guide, so read with caution.
The main story in "Grand Theft Auto 6" is full of fascinating characters, adrenaline-pumping missions, and twists and turns that often come out of nowhere. Even if you prioritize the story missions, you're still going to spend upwards of 75-80 hours completing it before you see the end credits roll. However, developer Rockstar Games has crafted the main story in "GTA 6" in a way that makes it so you can't just blow through every mission en route to the ending.
While the "GTA" franchise has always emphasized exploring detailed worlds, previous games have mostly allowed you to complete their main stories without partaking in too much side content. You could complete a story mission, wait for a few minutes, and then another would appear on the map, letting you bounce back and forth until you reached the end. In "GTA 6," no specific piece of content is forced upon you, but you also can't complete the main story without engaging with various parts of Leonida (where the game is set) first.
Rockstar Games Right from the start in "GTA 6," main story missions are somewhat drip-fed to you. You'll often have at least one story mission available to do on your map, but there are certainly times where there's nothing on your map aside from side activity icons and blacked-out locations that you haven't discovered yet. This mostly occurs after you've just completed a story mission, and it appears as though the game is hinting that you need to partake in some side content or world exploration to reach the next part of the story.
However, there are also several sections of the main story where the only way you can progress is engaging with non-story content. A prime example of this is when you're roughly 30% of the way through the story and make it to the Scarlet Motel in Port Gellhorn. Here, you get to fully play as Lucia for the first time, as Jason is recovering from an injury and can't get out of bed. In order to pay your rent at the motel, you need to go out and make some money as Lucia.
There's no dedicated main story mission to make the amount of money you need, so you're forced to figure out which side activities you want to do to bring in some cash. You can rob stores, deliver illegal goods to an NPC, or take part in a unique questline that's discovered by speaking to residents at the motel. Once you get the money you need and pay your rent, you can move on with the story. This is a major roadblock that halts all progress and forces you to participate in side activities and explore the map, though.
Rockstar Games Speaking of money, this is perhaps the whole crux of "GTA 6." While it's always an objective to earn money in "GTA" games, it's made clear that Jason and Lucia need a lot of money, and they won't get it all through the main story. From the side goal of putting money into your family BuckMe account to ensuring you have a stable life for the couple's son, Tommy, making money outside of the main story is consistently harped on throughout the game.
While some players might just want to get through the story as quickly as possible in "GTA 6," this gameplay loop was a great decision by Rockstar. It forces players to see more of Leonida, which leads them to discover interesting side content that is often worth doing, both in terms of money and overall enjoyment. You can still prioritize the main story missions, but you won't be able to reach the end credits without seeing some extra content in "GTA 6."

articles.t: Cyberleek Claims GTA 6 Xbox Build Leak | ShiftDelete.Net
articles.chapeau: The Cyberleek account says it leaked a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 on launch day and will release the executable on November 23. The threat is tied to…
articles.txt:
The anonymous Cyberleek account claims it dropped a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 on launch day and says it will release the game's executable on November 23, tying the leak to a memecoin.
The leaker behind months of GTA 6 spoilers is back. According to IGN , the online persona known as Cyberleek returned on November 19, the day GTA 6 launched, to drop what it claims is an Xbox build of the game without its executable file. Cyberleek now says it will release that executable as well.
In a statement reportedly published online, Cyberleek called the files a "full November 2026 build of GTA 6." It also predicted that the Xbox build would be used to emulate the game on PC "within a week, running far past 30fps." None of these claims has been verified, and IGN's report does not include a response from Rockstar.
As with its earlier leaks, Cyberleek has linked its threat to a cryptocurrency. It promised to release the executable immediately if its CyberLeek memecoin reaches a $15 million market cap. IGN reports that the news pushed the coin's value to $1.9 million, well short of that target. Cyberleek has said it will release the final file on November 23 either way.
Fans have been urging others not to put money into the coin. IGN notes that the leaker cashed out in August and again in October, and that an analysis of crypto transactions in late August suggested it had earned around $270,000.
Cyberleek first drew attention with a run of high-profile gameplay leaks in August, which led Take-Two to open an investigation and issue subpoenas to companies including Discord. At the time, Rockstar called the situation "heartbreaking" for its developers and "unfortunate" for fans, but kept the November 19 release date.
In October, Cyberleek tied more gameplay leaks to the coin's market cap and threatened to release a build of the game said to be over 200 GB if the coin hit $30 million. Some of those clips allegedly showed the lead characters fully naked, with NPCs not reacting, which led fans to suspect a developer menu or cheats rather than normal gameplay. Cyberleek also demanded a disc release and a public apology from Rockstar and Take-Two.
After its memecoin crashed, the account was thought to have gone quiet, until the launch-day post.
IGN points out that a full, recent build would be damaging for Rockstar and Take-Two, and would contradict the idea that Cyberleek only ever had access to an early development version. It is still unclear how the footage or any build left Rockstar, and whether the person or group behind the account can be identified may depend on how much information social networks and crypto exchanges are forced to hand over.
For players, the official game remains a console release for now. GTA 6 launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, with a 30fps target on consoles, and it topped $2.36 billion in launch-day sales according to Sensor Tower estimates . Rockstar has not announced a PC date, although a PC release has been reported for early 2027 .

articles.chapeau: Les missions de GTA 6 ne sont pas ma priorité car j'ai toujours une friperie à visiter dans les rues de Vice City.
articles.txt:
J'ai l'impression de vivre en plein délire en ce moment. GTA 6 est sorti ce jeudi 19 novembre à minuit et j’y ai joué pendant huit heures d’affilée, au nom d’un “ journalisme total ”. Pour être tout à fait honnête, j’ai fait une petite sieste vers 5 heures du matin, mais à part ça, j’ai travaillé très dur. J’ai désormais une nouvelle garde-robe et quelques inquiétudes concernant le prix des shorts en jean.
La plupart des joueurs auront passé leur toute première session du jeu à accomplir les missions, à explorer la carte et à découvrir dans quoi Jason et Lucia se sont fourrés. Pas moi. Mon objectif principal était de visiter autant de magasins que possible. 13 années sont passées depuis GTA 5 , je voulais voir ce qu’étaient devenues les collections pour hommes.
Lucia et Jason, les personnages principaux de Grand Theft Auto VI . © Rockstar Games Avant d’entrer dans le vif du sujet, sachez-le : vos vêtements ont plus d’importance que jamais par rapport aux autres opus de la saga Grand Theft Auto . Le nouvel “indice de recherche” permet aux flics de se souvenir de ce que vous portiez. Les semer ne signifie donc pas forcément que vous êtes tiré d’affaire. Changer de casquette ou de lunettes de soleil ne fera pas disparaître l’indice lié à vos vêtements non plus. Il faut complètement changer de tenue. Donc, techniquement, toutes ces virées shopping pourraient m’aider à m’en tirer à bon compte. C’est ma manière de justifier mes achats compulsifs, en tout cas.
Malheureusement, faire du shopping nécessite du cash , et au début, cela demande bien plus d’efforts que je ne l’avais espéré. On commence avec presque rien, et on passe une grande partie des premières heures à Key Lento, dans le comté marécageux de Mariana. Je m’étais lancé en pensant acheter des tonnes de vêtements. Au lieu de ça, j'ai dû vérifier ce que je pouvais me permettre.
Ma première occasion s’est présentée dans un magasin d’armes au hasard qui vendait également des vêtements de travail. J’ai rapidement jeté un œil, puis je me suis dirigé vers les shorts camouflage. En août dernier, la journaliste mode de GQ , Mahalia Chang, avait écrit dans un article que “les shorts camouflage étaient de retour, putain”, après avoir vu Jason en porter dans la bande-annonce. Qui étais-je pour la contredire ?
© Rockstar Games Non loin de là, à Hamlet, j’ai trouvé quelques friperies et j’ai déniché une veste de travail usée qui avait un petit air de Carhartt Detroit . Elle avait l’air bien usée, ce qui correspondait à la fois à mon budget et à l’état général de mon pick-up. J’ai aussi acheté une montre , mais j’y reviendrai une autre fois.
J'y suis allé à fond dans les recherches. J'ai comparé les articles, vérifié les prix et décidé de ce qui pouvait attendre. Il y avait des vêtements que je voulais et des vêtements que je pouvais m’offrir. Ce qui était agaçant, c’est que le jeu comprenait très bien la différence.
À un moment donné, j’ai acheté une casquette de camionneur et j’en étais très content. L’été dernier, j’avais écrit que je voulais leur donner une nouvelle chance, même si j’ai une tête que mes potes qualifient de “rêve de sniper”. Jason n’a pas ce problème (au sens figuré, en tout cas), alors j’ai pensé que je le laisserais en profiter.
© Rockstar Games Peu après, une bande de jeunes est venu me chercher des problèmes, m’a infligé quelques coups de poing et a fait tomber la casquette de sa tête. Je me suis enfui, et ce n’est qu’une fois en sécurité que je me suis rendu compte que je ne l’avais pas ramassée. J’avais à peine eu le temps d’en profiter. J’espère au moins que l’un d’entre eux la porte.
Après quelques missions, j’avais enfin assez d’argent pour me permettre une nouvelle virée shopping. Je suis monté dans ma camionnette cabossée et j’ai mis le cap sur le centre-ville, où les prix commençaient à devenir un peu plus élevés. Les vestes en jean tournaient autour de 140€. Un short en jean délavé foncé qui me plaisait beaucoup coûtait 50€, ce qui était légèrement plus que ce que je voulais dépenser. J’apprécie le fait que ce soit un jeu dans lequel on peut voler une voiture. Mais je me confrontais encore à un petit dilemme financier intérieur au sujet du prix d’un short. articles.t: Every Future Driving Game Needs to Steal This GTA 6 Feature
articles.chapeau: Playground, you have two months to put this in Forza Horizon 6 on PS5
articles.txt:
I've written numerous times about my love for open-world driving games. I love racing, but I also love cruising, taking in the landscape, setting out on road trips. My heart belongs to Test Drive Unlimited . I've written a tourist guide for the Forza Horizon series . One of my games of the year is the Road Trip DLC for American Truck Simulator .
Grand Theft Auto 6 has instantly joined my driving-game canon thanks to one tiny, but revolutionary, feature.
On the PlayStation 5 version of GTA 6 , Rockstar Games has come up with a genius application for the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers. When driving, the right trigger (the throttle) provides gentle resistance when cruising at the speed limit. The effect is a sort of soft stop for the trigger; your finger rests easily there, but it's also easy to push past it when you want to put your foot down.
I cannot overstate how much I love this. If you want to cruise, you no longer need to hover your finger in an approximate spot, making tiny adjustments to try to match speed with the traffic. You can just rest it against the soft stop, the way you just rest your foot on the accelerator pedal in a real car. It's so chill.
Image: Rockstar Games I don't always want to hurtle to my destination at full speed, even in a pure racing game like Forza. These beautiful open worlds are worth taking time to explore, seeing the sights and listening to the soothing drone of the engine. Sometimes tearing around everywhere at speed is noisy and stressful. In Forza Horizon, I adopt a more relaxed driving style by using manual gears and short-shifting to keep the revs low, but GTA 6 's solution is way more elegant.
The pleasure of cruising in GTA 6 is only enhanced by the richness of the world Rockstar has created. It's not just gorgeous, it's teeming with life, incidents (I watched a plane crash into the swamp while rolling on the freeway), and overheard conversations. And there are the radio stations to enjoy, too. Cruising the humid streets of the Keys while pumping Kaleidoscope FM is such a vibe.
I also enjoy this feature when I don't want to cruise, because pushing past the soft stop on the trigger is so deliciously satisfying. The amount of resistance is perfectly calibrated. It gives you the feeling of slamming your foot down to engage kickdown in a car with an auto gearbox and feeling the car surge forward. It's dramatic and cool.
I want this cruising-speed soft stop in every open-world driving game. For now, that sadly only means driving games on PS5, because Xbox gamepads don't have adaptive triggers. But Forza Horizon 6 is coming to PS5 on Jan. 26. Playground Games, you have two months to add this feature to the PS5 version of your game. If you manage it, I vow to buy a second copy and return to the roads of Japan, cruising my way to road-trip heaven.

articles.t: GTA 6 Crypto Token Looked Like a Launch-Day Hit: Who Was Really Buying?
articles.chapeau: A GTA 6 crypto token drew 3,903 SOL in its first hour. BitOK traced 95% of that buying to its own creator.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 Crypto Token Looked Like a Launch-Day Hit: Who Was Really Buying? Lockridge Okoth Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:29 PM GMT+1 2 min read SOL-USD -4.17% PUMP36507-USD -8.41% BIP-110. Photo by BeInCrypto Nearly 95% of a GTA 6 crypto token's first-hour buying came from wallets tied to its creator, according to a blockchain analytics report from BitOK shared with BeInCrypto exclusively. Outside buyers put in about 201 SOL and lost a quarter of it.
The token, Grand Theft Alleycat, launched on Thursday, Nov. 19, the day Rockstar Games set for the game's release. Traders chasing that hype were the target, because staged volume made the token look in demand.
The token was created on pump.fun, a site for launching Solana tokens in minutes. Buyers pay in SOL, Solana's native coin.
In the first hour, purchases reached 3,903 SOL. BitOK traced 3,454.8 SOL of that to 1,265 wallets funded by a single operator-controlled hub before they bought.
None of them sold. With the launch wallets and five other operator accounts added, nearly 95% of buying was the operator's own.
Nineteen wallets that bought the token at creation sold it for 3,202.8 SOL. BitOK says the operator was selling the token to itself.
The hub sent 10,795.5 SOL to a treasury wallet. That wallet held 3,856.24 SOL on Nov. 20, a balance BeInCrypto confirmed on-chain.
BitOK links the same operator to GTA6DOG (RICO), an Ethereum token whose code let its creator pull tokens from any wallet without permission. From Nov. 3 to 5, it emptied 10 buyers.
BitOK puts outside losses across both tokens at a preliminary $4,746. For Grand Theft Alleycat, that counts only the first hour of trading.
After that first hour, the price collapsed. GeckoTerminal data shows the token fell about 99.8% from its peak of roughly $0.001 and has barely traded since.
The trail runs through US exchanges. Network fees for the launches were paid with withdrawals from Coinbase and Kraken, alongside Bitget and SideShift. Another 41.99 ETH reached the HitBTC exchange.
No authority has charged anyone. BitOK, which sells address screening to exchanges and police, based its findings on wallet transfers.
GTA-themed tokens have burned traders before. The CYBERLEEK leak coin fell nearly 60% in August after its biggest spoiler.
On Nov. 20, the same signing keys launched two more tokens, Anthropic Cat Brian and iCat.
In May, South Korean prosecutors charged five people over a Solana meme coin rug pull.

Emmanuel Grégoire est accusé par plusieurs internautes d'avoir séché le Conseil de Paris du jeudi 19 novembre pour pouvoir jouer au nouveau GTA 6. L'élu répond.
C’est un buzz mondial auquel les politiques n’ont pas échappé : la sortie du nouveau jeu vidéo GTA 6 dans la nuit du mercredi 18 novembre vers minuit. Le maire de Paris, Emmanuel Grégoire, était lui aussi devant sa télévision et sa console pour découvrir ce jeu, attendu depuis plus de 13 ans .
Le maire de Paris s’est immortalisé sur Instagram dans son salon, avec en fond, le téléchargement de GTA 6. Le tout accompagné d’un message : « Let’s go ».
Certains utilisateurs font un parallèle étonnant le lendemain affirmant que l’édile a joué une partie de la nuit aux jeux vidéo avant de sécher le Conseil de Paris du jeudi 19 novembre. « C’est parce qu’ il a joué toute la nuit à GTA 6 qu’Emmanuel Grégoire a séché le Conseil de Paris ce matin ? », demande dès le lendemain le militant #SaccageParis Enzo Morel sur X avant de préciser qu’Emmanuel Grégoire est arrivé sur place vers 12 heures.
« Qui ici se pointe au boulot vers midi, sans remontrances ni perte de revenu ? », renchérit un autre internaute. Face à des publications qui cumulent des dizaines de milliers de vues sur les réseaux sociaux, le maire socialiste de Paris a répondu dans la soirée du jeudi 19 novembre.

articles.chapeau: GTA 6 a rapporté plus de 2,36 milliards de dollars en moins de 24 heures (24,59 millions d’exemplaires, selon Sensor Tower), près de trois fois le record de GTA V. Chiffres, audience et couacs.
articles.txt:
Moins de vingt-quatre heures après son lancement, Grand Theft Auto VI a rapporté plus de 2,36 milliards de dollars, avec 24,59 millions d’exemplaires vendus, selon les estimations du cabinet Sensor Tower. Le précédent record du premier jour, celui de GTA V en 2013, était de 800 millions de dollars. Le jeu est jouable en France depuis jeudi à minuit sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, à 79,99 € en édition Standard, et il existe aussi en version boîte chez Cultura .
Voici ce que disent les estimations de Sensor Tower, relayées jeudi par le site américain Deadline, qui s’ajoutent aux 17,07 millions de précommandes comptées avant la sortie :
Ni Rockstar ni Take-Two n’ont publié de chiffres officiels à ce stade : ce sont des estimations basées sur les boutiques numériques de Sony et Microsoft.
2,36 milliards de dollars en moins d’un jour : GTA V, avec ses 800 millions de dollars en 2013, était déjà le record du premier jour.
Une rue de Vice City, dans une image officielle du jeu. © Rockstar Games Un record d’audience sur Twitch, YouTube et Kick Le succès se mesure aussi devant l’écran. Selon Clubic, GTA 6 a atteint jusqu’à 7,9 millions de spectateurs simultanés sur l’ensemble des plateformes de streaming, dont plus de 3,3 millions sur Twitch, un record absolu pour un jeu. Sur Metacritic, le jeu affiche 99 sur 100 à partir d’environ 150 tests, une note égale à celle de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. En France, il est noté 10 sur 10 chez Gamekult, Gameblog et IGN France, et 19 sur 20 chez jeuxvideo.com.
Tout n’est pas parfait pour autant. Clubic relève deux pannes du PlayStation Network en douze heures, une indisponibilité du PlayStation Store en Europe jeudi matin et des plantages qui font perdre leur progression à certains joueurs, sans réaction officielle de Rockstar au moment de l’article. Le jeu tourne aussi à 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise, un choix assumé par Rockstar que beaucoup de tests critiquent.
Une poursuite de nuit dans Leonida. © Rockstar Games Pas de PC, pas d’Online : ce qu’il manque encore Au lancement, aucune version PC ni aucun mode multijoueur n’est disponible, et Rockstar n’a donné aucune date pour l’un comme pour l’autre. La boîte vendue en magasin ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement, et le jeu pèse jusqu’à 212 Go : prévoyez de la place avant d’acheter. Pour comparer les prix du jeu, voyez notre comparatif des meilleurs prix de GTA 6 , et pour la note record du jeu notre article sur le 99 sur Metacritic .
Cette estimation confirme ce que l’on pressentait : GTA 6 est le plus gros lancement de l’histoire du divertissement. Mais il faut garder deux nuances en tête. D’abord, les chiffres de Sensor Tower ne sont pas ceux de l’éditeur : ils reposent sur les boutiques numériques et ne comptent probablement pas tout ce qui se vend en magasin. Ensuite, un prix de 79,99 € à 99,99 € explique en partie le montant : avec un panier moyen d’environ 96 dollars par exemplaire (2,36 milliards divisés par 24,59 millions, notre calcul), l’édition Ultime pèse lourd.
Reste la vraie question pour les semaines à venir : la durée de vie du jeu. Sans mode en ligne ni version PC pour l’instant, le record du premier jour dira peu de chose sur la suite.
Pour acheter le jeu en boîte, rendez-vous sur la page GTA 6 PS5 de Cultura .

articles.txt:
Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days.
It was thought that the person or group responsible for the online Cyberleek persona had ended their spate of GTA 6 leaks last month, after their memecoin crashed despite efforts to boost its market cap.
In October, Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, and threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap. Gameplay clips reportedly leaked at the time allegedly showed Lucia fully naked — something that is not possible in the final launch version of the game.
Yesterday, November 19 — the GTA 6 release date — Cyberleek returned to drop a GTA 6 Xbox build without the game's executable. In a statement reportedly published online , Cyberleek claimed this Xbox build is a “full November 2026 build of GTA 6.” They predicted this Xbox build would be used to emulate GTA 6 on PC “within a week, running far past 30fps.”
The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.
Cyberleek has revived their crypto scheme, promising to release the executable immediately if it hits a $15 million market cap. While the CyberLeek memecoin was boosted in value by the news to $1.9 million yesterday, it is unlikely to get anywhere near the target.
Still, Cyberleek has vowed to release the final file anyway on November 23, whether the memecoin hits the market cap or not.
The release of a full and recent build of GTA 6 would of course be hugely damaging for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, which appears to have been unable to deter Cyberleek’s actions in any meaningful way since their spate of leaks began.
It would also run counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch.
Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000.
IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.
Cyberleek had threatened Rockstar and Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they failed to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of the memecoin hit $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam.
Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security.
In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.
Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible.

What is clear is that the stunt follows the same playbook Cyberleek has used since August, where each leak is tied to the price of a meme coin named after the leaker.

International Cyber Digest also reported that the same site is selling what it calls an older “development build” for $40 a download, which suggests the leak doubles as a sales pitch.

That gap is the whole story. The release arrives as Grand Theft Auto VI rolls out worldwide and as PC players ask the obvious question: could an Xbox build bring a playable PC port within reach? Cyberleek says yes, and says it could happen fast. Nothing in the coverage confirms that the build is genuine, complete, or runnable on a PC.
This analysis separates what outlets have reported from what Cyberleek has merely claimed. It also looks at why the timing matters, what the incentives behind the release look like, how the leak compares with Rockstar’s earlier security problems, and what readers should do (and avoid doing) while the story develops. Anything not backed by the reporting stays general here, and unconfirmed claims are labeled as such.

The label attached to the package reads “XBOX BUILD 1.0.2.1 (NOV 2026),” which points to a build made in the same month as the retail launch.
Reports put the download at approximately 209 GB. That is large enough to look like a real game package, though size alone proves nothing. A torrent of that weight could hold shipping assets, a mix of old and new data, or padding. Outlets have not verified the contents file by file, and no outlet in this coverage says it ran the build.
Coverage also attributes a line to Cyberleek, unconfirmed in its exact wording: “It is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build.” The phrase “this time” implies earlier releases, and it also implies that the group knows PC users are the audience that cares most. The reporting does not identify who Cyberleek is, how the group obtained the files, or whether it has any link to Rockstar’s staff or partners.
The naming of the game itself is inconsistent across the material. Outlets write GTA 6, GTA VI and Grand Theft Auto VI interchangeably, and this article follows suit. None of that affects the substance, but it explains why search traffic splits across several spellings today.
The table below sorts the claims by how well the coverage supports them. “Reported” means outlets describe it, not that they verified it. “Unconfirmed” means the claim comes from Cyberleek or from rumor and no outlet has tested it.
The pattern is easy to read. The facts that can be observed from outside (a torrent exists, it has a size and a label, it lacks an executable) are reported. Everything that would make the leak useful to a PC player is unconfirmed. That is a thin foundation for the “realistic PC port” framing that headlines have used.
A modern game package holds two broad kinds of material. Assets such as models, textures, audio and level data make up most of the bytes. The executable and its supporting code decide how those assets load, render and behave. Without the executable, a 209 GB pile of assets is closer to a very large archive than a game.
That is why reporting stresses the absence. Cyberleek has withheld the one file that would let anyone test the build, and the group has tied its release to conditions that benefit the group. Whether the executable exists in Cyberleek’s hands is not established. Whether it would run even if it did is a separate, equally open question.

GTA 6's Mandy Is Lexie Shoaibi: Actress Confirms Voice and Mocap Role for Viral Tenant - Shane the Gamer
articles.chapeau: Lexie Shoaibi has confirmed she plays Mandy, the flirty tenant from GTA 6's Pipework mission who took over social feeds within hours of the game's launch.
articles.txt:
You turn up to collect the rent. Instead you’re elbow-deep in a blocked sink while the tenant tells you you’re meant to be together. That’s Pipework, an early Jason mission in Grand Theft Auto VI, and the tenant at its centre now has a name and a face: Lexie Shoaibi confirmed in an Instagram post that she plays Mandy in Rockstar Games’ latest title.
Shoaibi said she provided both the voice and motion capture for Mandy, and LADbible reports the video went up on Thursday, 19 November. That’s launch day. Her line was simple: “I play Mandy,” followed by an invite for players to tell her if they’d found her in the game.
It isn’t just her word, either. According to ComicBook.com, Rockstar Games revealed who plays the character alongside the full cast on 19 November. Insider Gaming also points to the official GTA 6 cast list as naming Shoaibi.
That matters because the internet got there messily first. Insider Gaming notes that several people online have claimed that they are Mandy in GTA 6, but those claims are not the case. Now that both the cast list and the actress herself have confirmed it, that argument’s over.
The fan reaction has mostly been people jokingly picking Mandy over Jason’s actual partner:
Mandy’s screen time is short. GTABase describes her as one of Brian Heder’s tenants in the Leonida Keys, and she has a crush on Jason. She refuses to pay until he fixes her sink, and the mission becomes a plunger-and-wrench minigame while she keeps flirting.
If you’re hoping it goes somewhere, it doesn’t. Video Games Chronicle is blunt: Jason can’t romance Mandy, no matter how you approach the mission. PowerPyx’s walkthrough says the outcome is the same every time: Jason refuses her sexual advances, then she gets mad and tosses the cigar box out into the street.
There’s one small extra after the mission. Per VGC’s reporting, Jason gets a text message from Mandy saying she knows he wants her but can’t admit it. It’s flavour text. You can’t reply your way into a romance.
Here’s what makes the spike interesting. ComingSoon notes that Mandy’s popularity has emerged despite Rockstar not featuring her in any of the game’s trailers or promotional material. Years of trailer breakdowns, and the breakout character is a tenant with a clogged sink nobody had seen before.
LADbible collected some of the fan posts, including one that read “You can’t put Mandy in GTA VI and expect me to stay loyal to Lucia.” Vice reported that many players started searching whether it was possible “to cheat” on Lucia. The answer’s still no.
Our view: this is Rockstar doing what it always does. The marketing sells the leads, and then some one-scene weirdo steals the first weekend. GTA V had plenty of those. This time the meme machine just runs a lot faster.
Read also: GTA 6 Skips PC on November 19, but WoW: Forever and Warhammer Survivors Arrive This Month
Shoaibi’s a newcomer to games. ComicBook.com says this is the first video game Shoaibi has appeared in. Her screen work is a short list.
LADbible lists Paradise by the Dashboard Light (2016), The Good Fight (2017), Hollywood (2020) and Atom (2021), as well as voicing Dr. MedusaSaurus in the animated series Hamster & Gretel (2022–2023). That fits a familiar pattern. As ComicBook.com puts it, Rockstar Games often uses lesser-known acting talents, especially ones with no track record in video games.
It’s a casting approach that keeps Leonida from feeling like a celebrity cameo reel. It also means the people behind these characters can go from a handful of credits to the most-searched name in gaming overnight.
ComicBook.com floated the idea that her reception could change in the future, particularly with GTA Online content. That’s speculation. Rockstar hasn’t announced anything, and in the story as it stands, it appears players encounter Mandy only once.
If you ask us, a cameo in Online is the obvious move once the multiplayer side spins up. Rockstar has never been shy about bringing story favourites back. For now, Mandy lives in one Chapter 1 mission in Key Lento, plus one follow-up text, and you can replay it as often as you like.

We've yet to see confirmation that the build is genuine, but that could come as soon as tonight. If it is, it'll be anywhere between a few days or hours before the executable comes: According to Cyberleek's site, their crypto currently sits at a $1.83 million cap.
